_comment: Domain -> exogenous-predictor map for the Java forecast planner. `match_terms` select a domain bucket; predictors define curated economic relationships rather than text similarity. `role`, `concept` and `value_kind` are generic metadata consumed by the in-process Java model engine for quality checks, candidate evaluation and transparent driver reporting. `common_lags`, `preferred_frequency`, `preferred_series_hint` and `preferred_target_transformation` remain registry hints. English and folded Czech search terms support the mixed-language catalog without query-specific Java branches.

price_inflation.notes: Inflation is often affected by energy prices, FX, producer/import prices, wages and demand conditions with lags of a few months, and by monetary policy (rates) with longer lags.

predictors.search_query: policy interest rate central bank key rate urokova sazba repo sazba
energy price index electricity gas ceny energie elektrina plyn
wages earnings average wage index mzdy prumerna mzda
exchange rate euro dollar menovy kurz
food price index ceny potravin
services price index ceny sluzeb

policy_rate.notes: Central bank policy rates react to inflation and growth conditions and, with a lag, to FX and unemployment developments.

predictors.search_query: consumer price index inflation inflace spotrebitelske ceny
gdp growth rate real hruby domaci produkt hdp
exchange rate euro dollar menovy kurz
unemployment rate nezamestnanost

exports goods trade export vyvoz
exchange rate euro dollar menovy kurz

retail_sales.notes: Retail sales track real wages (purchasing power) and consumer confidence closely, and inflation/unemployment with a short lag.

banking_profitability.notes: Bank profitability is sensitive to the policy rate and loan volumes within a couple of quarters, and to credit costs (NPL) and the macro cycle (GDP, inflation) structurally.

loans outstanding volume credit uvery objem uveru
non-performing loans ratio nedobytne pohledavky
gdp growth rate real hruby domaci produkt hdp

gdp_growth.notes: GDP growth is a composite of industrial production, exports and retail sales in the short run, and is affected by unemployment structurally.

predictors.search_query: industrial production index prumyslova vyroba

retail sales trade maloobchod
unemployment rate nezamestnanost

wages.notes: Nominal wage growth follows inflation expectations and labour-market tightness (unemployment) and, structurally, productivity/GDP growth.

unemployment.notes: Unemployment lags the business cycle (GDP, industrial production) by a few months and is negatively related to wage growth and the policy rate over longer horizons.

equity_index.notes: Equity prices are sensitive to the policy rate and bond yields (discount-rate channel) and move with a benchmark index and market volatility.
